messages.text: morning. Grace and I are going to Bologna in early October, I want to get some Italian into my head before then
Lovely plan. How much Italian do you have right now, and how much time can you give it each day?
basically none, I can say grazie and that's it. I'm retired so time is fine, thinking 20 mins every morning with an app
Twenty minutes daily adds up fast, and mornings are a good habit slot. Do you want to focus on restaurant and travel phrases first?
yes exactly, ordering food, directions, hotel stuff. Grace wants me to do the talking, God help her
Ha, then ordering food is the right first target. Want a simple weekly plan: week one greetings and cafe orders, week two directions and numbers?
go on then
Week one: greetings, please and thank you, and ordering a coffee and a pastry. Do the app lesson each morning, and say the phrases out loud over breakfast. Does Grace want to join in?
she says she'll listen and correct me. she did french at school so she thinks she's an expert

recalls: What is Tom's plan for learning Italian before his trip?
Who is Tom travelling with and when?

messages.text: 5 days in a row now! app says I have a streak
Five mornings straight is a solid start. Can you order a coffee in Italian yet, ahead of the Bologna trip in October?
un caffè per favore, yes. also I found a conversation class, Thursday evenings at the community centre, starts 3rd Sept
That's a great complement to the app, since you'll actually be speaking. Is it for beginners, and will you go?
beginners, 7 to 8:30. I'm signing up tonight. nervous about talking in front of strangers, funny for an ex teacher
Plenty of teachers dread being the student. You'll have 20 minutes of app practice behind you each morning, which helps. Want a few phrases for introducing yourself?
yes please. also I need to go to the allotment later, beans want picking
Sounds like a good Sunday. Are those the runner beans? Here's a start: mi chiamo Tom, sono di Leeds, sono in pensione. That last one means I'm retired.
yes runner beans, loads of them. and courgettes, but they're sulking. sono in pensione, I like that

recalls: What Italian classes or practice does Tom do?

messages.text: big news. Hannah had the baby on Saturday, a girl, Ada. my first grandchild!
Congratulations Tom, what wonderful news! How are Hannah and Ada doing, and how are you and Grace feeling?
both fine, tired. Grace is over the moon. they live in Manchester so we'll be going over most weekends to help
That's lovely, you'll be very welcome. Does that change anything for the Bologna trip in early October?
yeah. we've decided to move it to spring. no way I'm missing Ada's first weeks
That makes complete sense, and it gives you more months to practise Italian. Do you have a spring month in mind?
April probably. I went to my first class Thursday by the way, it was fine! I did the whole intro, mi chiamo Tom
Well done, that's the hardest bit done. Is the class staying on Thursday evenings, and are you keeping up the morning app sessions?
yes to both, though weekend mornings in Manchester might be tricky

recalls: What is Tom growing at his allotment?
Where does Tom spend his weekends?

messages.text: back from Manchester. Ada is tiny and perfect. I held her for an hour
That sounds like a lovely weekend. Did you get any Italian in, or was it all baby duty?
did the app on the train, 20 mins, kept the streak going. then allotment this afternoon, depressing
Good train use of time. What was depressing about the allotment, the courgettes again?
yep. three tiny courgettes all season. the slugs and the weather won. runner beans did great though
A good bean year at least. Will you try courgettes again next year, or give the space to something else?
I'm done with courgettes. not worth the bother. thinking garlic for winter instead
Garlic is a sensible swap, it gets planted in autumn and mostly looks after itself. Do you want a rough planting timetable for Leeds?
yes please, I think Oct to Nov for the cloves right?
That's right, October into November works well. Plant cloves pointy end up, about 15cm apart and a few cm deep. Do you have a bed cleared yet?

recalls: What does Tom do on Wednesdays?

messages.text: I've been asked to volunteer at the library homework club, Wednesdays 3:30 to 5. thought I'd say yes, miss the classroom a bit
Sounds like a natural fit for a retired teacher. Which subjects will you help with, and when does it start?
mostly maths and english, ages 11 to 14. starting next Wednesday
That's your old territory. With the Thursday class and weekends in Manchester, how is your week shaping up?
busy! Wednesday club, Thursday Italian class, weekends at Hannah's. the app is slipping, I missed three mornings this week
Understandable with a new grandchild. Would a shorter session help, or is the app starting to feel like a chore?
honestly the app is getting boring. same drills, a cartoon owl nagging me. I like the class more
The class sounds like it works better for you. Do you want to think about what else could replace the 20 minutes in the morning?
maybe. let me think

recalls: Is Tom still using the Italian app?
What did Tom start at the library?

messages.text: first homework club done. a girl asked me to explain fractions and I forgot how much I enjoy it
That's great, Tom. Did the club run the way you hoped, and are you going back next Wednesday?
definitely. also I've deleted the app. been looking for another way to learn Italian
A bold move after a long streak. What did you have in mind, since the Thursday class stays?
Grace found me a simple Italian novel, a short one for learners with an English glossary. reading 20 mins each morning instead
Same 20 minutes, but reading something with a story is more fun than drills. Are you managing it with a dictionary, or guessing from context?
a bit of both. I wrote new words in a notebook like I used to make the kids do
Very teacherly. Want to bring five words from your notebook to the Thursday class to practise using them out loud?
good idea, will do

recalls: When is Tom's trip to Bologna now planned?

messages.text: can you help me sort out my week, it's getting crowded
Of course. What do you have fixed so far?
Wed homework club 3:30 to 5, Thursday Italian class 7 to 8:30, weekends in Manchester with Ada. mornings are novel time
Does that leave a regular slot for the allotment? Your garlic needs planting in October.
Monday and Tuesday are free so allotment on Monday. I'll buy the garlic cloves this week
Monday for the allotment is a good plan. And the trip: are you still looking at April for Bologna with Grace?
yes, april, I'd like to book the flights soon though. Grace wants to avoid Easter crowds
Good thinking, mid-April after Easter could suit you both. Should I help you compare dates, or wait until Hannah's plans settle?
wait a bit. but I'm on chapter 4 of the novel, understood a whole page without the glossary!

recalls: What is Tom growing or planning to grow at the allotment?
What is Tom doing for Italian practice now?

messages.text: garlic is in! did four rows on Monday, 40 cloves
Nice work, that should give you a good crop. Do you have anything else on the plot, apart from the runner beans clearing out?
just clearing the bean plants now. no courgettes next year, I've decided. maybe more beans
Beans were your success this year, so that's a sound choice. How's the Italian going with the novel?
chapter 7. still do the Thursday class and I ordered a whole lunch in Italian at the cafe near the library, Grace was proud
That's real progress, and exactly what you'll want in Bologna. Did the homework club kids hear about it too?
ha yes, one asked me to teach her 'buongiorno'. Ada's smiling now too, Hannah sent a video
What a lovely week. Do you want to start a rough list of places for the April trip, or enjoy Ada's smiles for now?
list please, Grace wants food markets first

portrait: Tom is a 58-year-old retired secondary-school teacher in Leeds, married to Grace. He is learning Italian for a spring (April) trip to Bologna, now practising by reading a simple Italian novel each morning and attending a Thursday-evening class. He is a new grandfather to Ada, spends weekends in Manchester, volunteers at the library homework club on Wednesdays, and has planted garlic on his allotment.
